look_here_first: Follow a trailing or arching cane and find the backward-curved prickles. Then inspect the alternate 3–5-foliolate leaves with stipules, the white 5-petaled flower with a shallow hypanthium and many stamens/pistils, and finally the black aggregate fruit made of many tiny drupelets.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: woody trailing/arching bramble forming low tangles or thickets

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: stems with backward-curved to straight prickles

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: leaves alternate, stipulate, usually 3–5 foliolate and appearing palmately compound

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: white radial flower with 5 petals and a shallow dish-like hypanthium

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: 100+ free stamens in detailed local treatment

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: many free superior pistils on a conic receptacle

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: aggregate fruit composed of many fleshy one-stoned drupelets

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: ripe aggregate fruit black with dark red juicy pulp

key_traits.label: Stem
key_traits.text: Tough trailing/arching canes bear broad-based prickles; use this with leaf and fruit characters rather than calling every thorny vine a Rubus.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Alternate, stipulate, 3–5-foliolate leaves with serrate leaflets; prickles may occur on petiole/rachis as well as stems.

key_traits.label: Flower
key_traits.text: Five white petals, five reflexed sepals, numerous free stamens, and many separate superior pistils sit on/inside a shallow hypanthium.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Each flower produces an aggregate of roughly a dozen to several dozen fleshy drupelets; each drupelet contains a hard stone.

key_traits.label: Family training
key_traits.text: Excellent Rosaceae anchor because it shows stipules + hypanthium + many stamens + many free carpels + aggregate fruit in one local plant.
